thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> HIGH: hydra-enterprise (EU1) p99 latency > SLO (currently 1.8s, SLO 1.0s). Auto-psm triggered.

Sara (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at consoles now.

Raj: Noticed a sustained p95/p99 spike starting ~+8m. Could be a tenant traffic storm or garbage collection across the dedicated pool. Pulling tenant heatmap.

Mike: I see Hydra-Enterprise's dedicated pool CPU pinned on GPU nodes 3/5 in eu1-west. KV cache miss rate jumped 4x. Investigating tail latencies.

Elaine: CS says customer reports slow API responses and some timeouts on large chat sessions. Amy, any direct comms?

Amy (CS): Sent a short note to their SRE lead, asked for whether they changed traffic patterns. Waiting reply.

Sara (oncall): From our metrics: p95 850ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.1s -> 1.8s. Error rate is slightly up (0.2% -> 0.9%) but mainly high tail. Logs show a few 502s on model proxy.

Raj: Tenant heatmap: one tenant (hydra-analytics) accounts for 68% of tokens in the pool over last 10m; aggressive long-context jobs. This tenant shares the same dedicated capacity. Suspect noisy neighbor.

Mike: Agree. Propose tenant isolation (move hydra-analytics to warm spare) and scale dedicated pool by +2 nodes temporarily. Which is faster?

Sara (oncall): Evicting/moving tenant has lower risk to other customers if we do a graceful redirect. Scaling nodes will take ~6-9 minutes to be effective. Eviction + redirect might be 2-3 minutes if infra-runner can apply route.

infra-runner: Standby to execute. To move tenant we need to update routing tag and bump their pool affinity. Recommended steps: 1) update routing to warm-spare eu1-b, 2) spin up a pre-warmed instance for hydra-analytics if not already, 3) monitor KV cache pressure.

Raj: Prep command to isolate tenant (dry-run first):

```
# Dry-run: simulate routing change
redwoodctl route simulate --tenant hydra-analytics --target eu1-b-warm
```

When green:

```
redwoodctl route set --tenant hydra-analytics --target eu1-b-warm --grace 30s
```

Mike: I'll kick scale while we do the move. Running autoscale override +2 nodes on eu1-dedicated pool.

Mike: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rwd-eu1-dedicated --desired-capacity 12` (already triggered). Confirmed request submitted.

incident-bot: Runbook step 3 started: Tenant isolation requested by sara (oncall). PagerDuty updated.

Sara (oncall): Amy, please tell the customer we're performing a targeted mitigation (isolating heavy sub-tenant) and may redirect some requests briefly. We'll confirm progress in 10 minutes.

Amy (CS): Sending now.

Elaine: Quick check: any model version rollouts recently? We had a staged quantized kernel update in eu1 two hours ago for a different pool — not this one per release notes.

Raj: No config changes for hydra-enterprise tenant. Traffic spike + long context sessions.

Mike: infra-runner, please run the simulate command then apply when green. I'll monitor scale events and proxy logs.

infra-runner: Simulate success, latency impact projection looks good. Applying routing change now with 30s grace.

infra-runner: `redwoodctl route set` returned OK. Redirecting ~70% of hydra-analytics traffic to eu1-b-warm.

Sara (oncall): Seeing p99 drop begin at +45s after route. p99: 1.8s -> 1.25s. p95 back to 900ms. Error rate stabilizing.

Mike: Autoscale nodes reported in progress; expected readiness in ~6m. But isolation already brought most of the tail down.

incident-bot: Post-mitigation check scheduled in 5m. Please add any follow-ups.

Raj: Recommend we keep hydra-analytics isolated until end-of-day and run a capacity planning review. Also suggest we enable tenant-level KV cache reservations to prevent single-tenant cache trashing.

Elaine: +1 on cache reservations. Add a follow-up ticket for Optimize to propose a quantization/segmentation profile per tenant.

Amy (CS): Customer update: "Thanks, latency improved noticeably. We'll throttle a subset of our analytics jobs until tomorrow morning." They asked for a post-incident summary.

Sara (oncall): Owners and action items:
- Sara (oncall): Incident commander, keep monitoring, confirm SLA breach window.
- Raj: Create incident root cause notes and tenant heatmap export.
- Mike: Verify autoscale and instance health, ensure warm-spare is stable.
- Elaine: Add follow-up ticket for cache reservations and policy.
- Amy (CS): Draft post-incident summary and coordinate with customer.

Raj: Quick RCA hypothesis: Noisy neighbor (hydra-analytics long-context batch jobs) caused KV cache pressure + dispatcher queueing, yielding p99 spike. Isolation mitigated impact.

Sara (oncall): SLA calculations: initial breach window ~10:13:22 -> 10:21:05 UTC (observed p99 > 1.0s). We'll compute exact weighted violation for billing and SLO dashboard.

incident-bot: Incident state updated -> mitigated. Severity downgraded to MEDIUM.

Mike: All infra checks green. Warm-spare reported 98% health. Autoscale finished, cluster now at desired capacity.

Elaine: Logging follow-ups: collect KV cache metrics at 1s granularity during incident and save to incident artifacts.

Sara (oncall): Great. I'll keep this thread open for wrap-up. If no further regressions in 30m, we'll close and publish postmortem draft.

Amy (CS): Customer confirmed no further issues after redirect. They're fine with a postmortem and capacity plan.

Raj: Exported heatmap + logs to /artifacts/incidents/5298765432/. Added preliminary notes.

Sara (oncall): Closing note: Good coordination. Isolation + scaling is our standard play for dedicated pool noisy neighbors — consider automating isolation runbook next quarter. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation (monitoring mode).
